purpose: Teach: 茶碗/はさみ/出掛ける/短冊/さくらんぼ/あゆ/前歯/ヤリ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、お茶碗、絶対、特注で、絶対、作ったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, do you remember? When you were young, your father had a rice bowl made specially for him. I remember it so clearly.
lines.style: Soft opening, nostalgic. Gaze turned inward. Warm certainty in the memory — not asking if she remembers, but inviting her to travel back with him. Gentle pace, no rush.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの、絶対、お裁縫の、絶対、はさみ、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、研いでくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I do. And do you remember? Your grandfather used to sharpen my sewing scissors for me when we were young. I kept them so carefully.
lines.style: Reciprocal warmth. Eyes brightening at the memory. Speaking more to the memory itself than to him. Soft lift at the end — matching his gentleness with her own. A slight hum of contentment beneath the words.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さんと、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、よく、絶対、温泉に、絶対、出掛ける、絶対、わよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Remember how often we'd all go to the hot springs together back then? Your father and you and me. It felt like there was always time for it.
lines.style: A small smile in the voice. Slower pace — lingering on the image. The faintest sigh of wistfulness that something so natural then feels precious now. Not regretful, just aware.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お孫さんの、絶対、短冊、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、大切に、絶対、しまっていたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I do remember. And your grandson's tanzaku — I kept them so carefully, didn't I? I still have them all put away.
lines.style: Tender pride in her voice. She's speaking a truth she's held onto. Deliberate, unhurried. A quiet note of care in how she says 'carefully' — this mattered to her, it still does.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お庭の、絶対、さくらんぼ、絶対、お父さん、絶対、収穫したぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: The cherry trees in the garden — your father picked those cherries. Do you remember, Gran?
lines.style: Reaching back into the specific image. Quieter here, more intimate. Seeking confirmation not because he doubts, but because sharing the memory matters. A thread of delight in his voice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、川で、絶対、あゆ、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、釣ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I do. And don't you remember? Your grandfather caught sweetfish in the river that summer. Such a patient fisherman he was.
lines.style: Animated but unhurried. She's moved by his memory, moves to her own. A gentle pride in speaking of her husband. The words carry the weight of someone who watched him do these things with attention.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お孫さんの、絶対、前歯、絶対、抜けた時、絶対、お父さん、絶対、嬉しかったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When your grandson lost his first tooth, I remember how happy your father was. He was truly delighted.
lines.style: A smile breaks through — the sudden, simple joy of a memory that still warms him. Quicker than before, lighter. The affection for that moment is still alive in his voice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、ヤリ、絶対、投げ、絶対、競技、絶対、得意だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: And your grandfather was so good at javelin, wasn't he? Truly skilled. I loved watching him throw.
lines.style: Softest voice yet. Speaking with the certainty of someone who witnessed it many times. A tender admiration — not just remembering the fact, but remembering how it felt to see him do it. Voice trails slightly, held by the image.
